question: Which local groups do midwives in Nigeria often work with to boost maternal health programs?

options.A: Market women associations and traditional rulers
options.B: Commercial transport unions and highway patrol units
options.C: International donor agencies and foreign volunteers
options.D: Secondary school athletic clubs and debating societies

explanation: Local leaders and women's groups have a lot of influence in the community, making them great partners for public health outreach. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is waiting for patients to come to the clinic often less effective than actively going into the community?

options.A: It requires more financial funding from the local government council
options.B: It fails to build local ownership and long-term trust in health programs
options.C: It causes immediate shortages of essential obstetric drugs in the clinic
options.D: It prevents midwives from administering routine immunizations to children

explanation: When people are involved in their own healthcare, they care more about the program and keep up healthy habits over time. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which community mobilization technique uses local storytelling and performance?
explanation: Cultural performances grab people's attention and share health messages clearly using familiar languages and styles. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h2)

question: A midwife wants to talk to busy traders about antenatal care. Where is the best place to find them?
explanation: Going straight to busy trading spots lets the midwife meet many women where they already gather. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the main job of Village Health Workers in community healthcare?

options.A: Managing financial budgets for state ministry headquarters
options.B: Providing continuous health education between formal clinic visits
options.C: Importing foreign pharmaceutical drugs for local distribution
options.D: Performing major surgical operations in primary health centers

explanation: Village Health Workers connect the clinic to families far away by giving helpful advice and support day-to-day. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why does scheduling outreach visits on local market days help get more people to attend?

options.A: It allows midwives to sell medical equipment to traders for profit
options.B: It stops all farming activities until the healthcare program ends
options.C: It respects the community's economic routine and ensures higher attendance
options.D: It guarantees that government officials will provide free transport

explanation: Fitting health activities around people's daily routines means they do not have to choose between work and healthcare. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why is it important to teach women about pregnancy danger signs?

options.A: Allowing them to perform caesarean sections without medical training
options.B: Replacing the need for professional midwives entirely in rural clinics
options.C: Empowering them to manufacture their own antibiotic medications
options.D: Enabling them to demand prompt medical attention during emergencies

explanation: Knowing the warning signs helps women and their families act fast when something goes wrong. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h4)

question: How do cooperative savings schemes help improve maternal health outcomes?

options.A: They remove the need for antenatal checkups at primary health centers
options.B: They reduce transport delays caused by a lack of funds during obstetric emergencies
options.C: They eliminate all medical complications associated with multiple births
options.D: They provide free medical degrees to pregnant women in rural areas

explanation: Having money saved up helps families pay for transport and treatment quickly during an emergency. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to community health participation?

options.A: Deep-seated traditional beliefs and cultural practices
options.B: Mistrust of the formal health sector and language differences
options.C: Excessive availability of trained resident obstetricians in rural clinics
options.D: Gender power dynamics and male household gatekeepers

explanation: Rural areas usually suffer from a shortage of skilled staff, so having too many obstetricians is not a real barrier. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why is it better to work along with traditional birth attendants instead of ignoring them?

options.A: They manage the financial budget of the local government health department
options.B: They are legally certified to perform major surgical procedures in teaching hospitals
options.C: They supply the primary health center with advanced laboratory testing kits
options.D: They hold significant influence over community choices and can become effective referral agents

explanation: Building a good relationship with traditional birth attendants encourages them to send complicated cases to the clinic early. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the best way to tell if a community health mobilization program has truly worked?

options.A: The volume of medical textbooks stored in the health center office
options.B: The frequency of meetings held by foreign donor agencies
options.C: Sustainable changes in health behaviors and increased facility utilization
options.D: The total number of educational posters printed and distributed

explanation: Real success shows up when people actually change their health habits and keep using the clinic services. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h6)

question: A midwife wants to review a recent safe motherhood campaign with the local villagers. What should she do?

options.A: Review the financial accounts of the local government chairman in secret
options.B: Submit a private report to the international donor without speaking to villagers
options.C: Invite community members to share their perspectives on the program's successes and challenges
options.D: Count the number of empty drug cartons left inside the clinic store room

explanation: Including community members in the review ensures their feedback helps shape future health programs. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h6)
